name: BWA Wrocław
funding: Municipal gallery network of the City of Wrocław.
records_note: Its public bulletin posts annual reports 2021 to 2025 naming grant funders; budget shares only, no full accounts, and no governing board is listed.

name: Smena Centre for Contemporary Culture
watch: Bookshop, gallery and festival; integrated the Bulat Galeev 'Prometheus' foundation in 2023; co-produces a 2026 show with Zarya in Vladivostok.
records_note: No official website for Smena could be found, so none of the four could be checked; press says it has no annual budget.

name: Ploshchad Mira Museum Centre
funding: Regional state (Ministry of Culture of Krasnoyarsk Krai); subsidy of 40–50m RUB a year was 70–80% of budget in 2019, rest from earnings, grants and unnamed local business.
watch: Runs the Krasnoyarsk Museum Biennale since 1995; director Olga Temnikova since 2023; named Cosmoscow 'Museum of the Year' 2025.
records_note: A regional budget museum: its Documents page posts public reports 2016 to 2025 and balance sheets 2023 and 2024; no funder list or board.

name: Arsenal, Volga-Vyatka branch of the Pushkin Museum
funding: Federal via the Pushkin State Museum of Fine Arts (branch since 2020); three-year cooperation agreement with Nizhny Novgorod region signed 15 Nov 2024.
watch: Founder-director Anna Gor became a Pushkin deputy director; Alexander Komarov now heads the branch.
records_note: A federal branch with no reports of its own; its Support page names sponsors and patrons. The Pushkin Museum parent site could not be read.

name: Tikhaya Studio
funding: Artist-run autonomous non-profit founded 2015 by Artem Filatov; grants, ticket/catalogue sales and donated artworks; a Garage Museum grant funds its archive.
watch: Nine resident artists; collaborates with Garage on archiving the Nizhny Novgorod scene.
records_note: This artist-run studio's site names its team and takes donations but posts no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board.

name: PERMM Museum of Contemporary Art
funding: Regional state (GKBUK; founder Ministry of Culture of Perm Krai); founded 2009 under governor Chirkunov with Marat Gelman and sponsor Sergei Gordeev; new building on Krisanova St since 2024.
watch: FSB searched the museum and director Nailya Allakhverdieva's home on 21 Nov 2024 in the 'terrorism justification' case against founder Gelman (declared foreign agent 2021, listed as terrorist/extremist 2024); museum closed one day. Prosecutor filed a conflict-of-interest suit against the director in Oct 2024; an earlier search in Mar 2024. Allakhverdieva left; Elena Novikova appointed.
records_note: A regional state museum: its Documents page posts results reports 2019 to 2025 with a balance sheet; it names no funders and no board.

name: Perm State Art Gallery
funding: Regional state (GKBUK; founder Ministry of Culture of Perm Krai); new 21,000 sq m building in the Zavod Shpagina cluster financed by the region, move completed Feb 2026.
watch: Director Yulia Tavrizyan; sponsor list not published on the site.
records_note: Posts a 2025 results report and 2025 financial results report, with plans back to 2022; no sponsor list and no board.

name: Erarta Museum of Contemporary Art
funding: Private: founded 2010 by Marina Varvarina (widow of Orimi tea-and-coffee group owner Dmitry Varvarin); the museum states it has never taken state support, grants or sponsors.
watch: 12,000 sq m, c. 40 exhibitions a year; c. US$30–35m invested in the building. No sanctions match for Varvarina on OpenSanctions.
records_note: The museum states it takes no state money, grants or sponsors; its site posts no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board.

name: Manege Central Exhibition Hall
funding: City: St Petersburg state budgetary institution under the Committee for Culture; director Anna Yalova (acting from Sep 2022, confirmed Feb 2023).
watch: Site has no partners page; 2024 shows (Pushkinskaya-10 retrospective, Polytechnic Museum) credited to the Committee for Culture.
records_note: Names partners and sponsors in text with no date and lists a four-member supervisory board; posts only a 2025 task report and a financial plan.

name: Pushkinskaya-10 Art Centre
funding: Self-managed non-state artists' commune (since 1989) housing 14 galleries, studios and clubs; funding sources not published.
watch: A 2024 retrospective at the city's Manege was supported by the Committee for Culture; residencies 'White Noise' and St Petersburg Art Residency run on site.
records_note: Its People page has a board (Pravlenie) group, but it posts no annual reports, accounts or funder list.

name: Zarya Centre for Contemporary Art
funding: Private: founded 2013 by Alexander Mechetin, founder and co-owner of spirits group Novabev (ex-Beluga Group) — alcohol money, allowed.
watch: Announced in 2020 that main activity would shift to the Golubitskoye estate (Krasnodar), but the Vladivostok residency (2025 open call) and exhibitions (Sept 2026–Apr 2027 show with Smena) continue. OpenSanctions finds no entry for Mechetin.
records_note: Its partners page shows undated logos under three headings; the site posts no reports, accounts or board, and names no legal entity.

name: Kramskoi Voronezh Regional Art Museum
funding: Regional state (Voronezh Oblast); director Yulia Zaichenko; partners named are other state museums.
watch: Voronezh's independent VCCA lost its premises in 2019.
records_note: It posts yearly reports 2020 to 2024 and annual financial plans 2022 to 2025, but names no funders and shows no board.
